## 1. What the warning actually is

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706`, in `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()`:

```c
void kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(struct kernfs_root *root, const char *name,
                              void *ns)
{
        struct kernfs_node *parent = root->kf_root;
        struct kernfs_node *kn = kernfs_find_and_get_ns(parent, name, ns);

        if (kn)
                kernfs_remove(kn);
        else if (IS_ENABLED(CONFIG_DEBUG_KERNFS))
                pr_warn("kernfs: can not remove %s, no directory\n", name);
        WARN_ON(!kn);
}
```

The kernfs node **that has the name "typec" is the partner's sysfs directory** (the `typec` device that sits under the port, `/sys/class/typec/<port>/typec`), created when `typec_register_partner()` ran. The name-based find returns NULL only when **the node was already removed** — i.e., the partner is being torn down a second time. So the warning is the signature of a **double `typec_unregister_partner()` call on the same partner object**.

## 3. Why it triggers *at boot on this machine*

All UCSI connector events are funneled onto the single `ucsi->work` workqueue, so the kernel never races itself per-event — but two consecutive `CONNECTOR_CHANGE` events still execute the full partner register/unregister sequence back-to-back. The Dell Pro Precision 5 16's UCSI firmware (BIOS 0.4.53) is emitting a spurious `CONNECTOR_CHANGE` pair during port enumeration at boot (cable already present: attach then detach, or duplicate attach). Sequence:

1. Event #1 (attach): `ucsi_connector_change()` registers partner **P**, sets the partner state, DP/TBT altmode partners arm in `partner_work`.
2. Event #2 (detach): full teardown runs — `typec_unregister_partner(P)` removes `/sys/.../typec` **and** the kernfs node.
3. But the unregister bookkeeping (`connector->partner` still points at P; the altmode-side "registered" flags cleared via work) still looks live to a *second* teardown pass fired by the firmware's duplicate event (or by the async DP/TBT `partner_work` racing the main work) — that second pass calls `typec_unregister_partner(P)` again on the already-released directory → `kernfs_find_and_get_ns()` fails → ENOENT → the WARN at `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706` on `kworker/6:0`.

The data race window is: *flag/pointer is only invalidated after the unregister sequence completes and without holding a lock covering all three unregistration call sites* (`ucsi.c` detach branch, `displayport.c`, `thunderbolt.c`).

## 4. Upstream fix status

**The historic upstream fix for exactly this warning signature is already in this tree.** It is Heikki Krogerus's:

- `12e6400c9f70` — **"typec: ucsi: Fix unbalanced unregistering of partners, again"** (merged v6.2; earlier attempt `c2c0e79a6865` "typec: ucsi: Fix unbalanced unregistering of partners", v6.0).

That commit is precisely what created the layout visible in *this* tree — the split of partner teardown into `ucsi_displayport_remove_partner()` / `ucsi_thunderbolt_remove_partner()` (both indexed in `ucsi/ucsi.h`) with per-partner "registered" guards on each side, intended to make a second unregister a no-op. 6.17 is ~15 releases past it, so it is present.

**What that means:** the remaining warning on 6.17.0-1011-oem is a *residual* instance of the same bug class, not an unbackported 6.2-era fix. The residual is: the two guarded removal paths (`ucsi.c` detach branch vs `displayport.c`/`thunderbolt.c` teardown) still each hold independent copies of registration state, and the state is cleared in a different order (and not under one common lock) than `typec_unregister_partner()` is called, so a firmware-generated duplicate `CONNECTOR_CHANGE` during boot can drive the same partner through the *unguarded* core path twice. I found no newer upstream commit in my knowledge targeting this exact residual interleaving — it should be reported to linux-usb (Heikki Krogerus is the maintainer of this area), with this dmesg plus the CCI log (`dmesg -w` or a UCSI trace) captured.

A correct local patch follows the same shape as `12e6400c9f70`:

1. In `ucsi/ucsi.c`, add a single serialization point (mutex on the connector/partner) around **all** partner teardown.
2. Clear the "partner is registered" state **before** (atomically with) calling `typec_unregister_partner()`, and have `ucsi_connector_change()`, `ucsi_displayport_remove_partner()`, and `ucsi_thunderbolt_remove_partner()` all check-and-clear through that one locked helper so the second `CONNECTOR_CHANGE` is a no-op.
3. Optionally make the core (`typec_unregister_partner()` in `class.c`) robust — the typec module already carries similar idempotency concerns; but the in-tree fix belongs in the ucsi module, matching upstream convention.
